name: Denomination Effect
description: People are less willing to spend an equivalent amount of money when it is held in one large denomination than when it is split into smaller units. Large bills feel less 'spendable' and can function like a soft self-control device.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to wallets, stored-value balances, reward credits, gift cards, budgeting tools, and checkout design: the form in which money is represented changes spending behavior even when the total value is identical.
prevalence_note: Known in consumer-behavior, pricing, payments, and fintech-adjacent discussions, but not a baseline named law in general interaction-design practice.

findings.description: Across consumer-spending studies, people were less likely to spend an equivalent amount of money when it was represented as one large denomination rather than several smaller ones, implying that denominations are not treated as fully fungible and can serve as self-control devices.
